title: Responder Evidence and Status Playbook: bridge scripts, escalation ladder, and customer templates
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview
-------
This playbook standardizes evidence collection, escalation sequencing, bridge setup, and external status messaging for multi-service incidents affecting Redwood Inference production environments. It is intended for first responders, bridge operators, incident commanders, and Customer Success representatives.

Purpose and scope
- Reduce time-to-evidence to 15 minutes for P0/P1 incidents.
- Provide ready-to-send customer status templates for common impact classes.
- Define clear escalation paths between on-call engineers, SRE, product owners, and executive contacts.
- Apply to hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment incidents that require cross-functional coordination.

Audience
- Primary: oncall engineers, bridge operators, SREs.
- Secondary: customer success, solutions engineering, legal (for escalations involving contracts).

Roles and responsibilities
- First Responder (FR): Acknowledge page, run immediate triage checklist, collect ephemeral evidence, stand up the bridge if required.
- Bridge Operator (BO): Manage the conference bridge, coordinate status cadence, control access to the bridge notes doc.
- Incident Commander (IC): Owns incident timeline, decisions and customer statements until handoff.
- Service Owner (SO): Provides technical diagnosis, mitigations and rollout plan.
- Customer Success Lead (CSL): Sends customer-facing notices and tracks SLAs/credits required.

Severity classification (quick reference)
| Severity | Impact criteria | Target ack | Bridge required? | Customer notice cadence |
|----------|-----------------|------------:|------------------:|------------------------:|
| P0       | Platform-wide outage, >50% customer errors/traffic loss | 1 min | Yes | Start at 15m, update every 30m |
| P1       | Significant degradation for a subset of customers or models | 5 min | Yes | Start at 30m, update hourly |
| P2       | Single-customer major impact or degraded latency beyond threshold | 15 min | Conditional | Start at 60m or on request |
| P3       | Minor functional issues or workarounds available | 60 min | No | Weekly summary or on resolution |

Immediate evidence collection checklist (First 10 minutes)
1. Capture monitoring snapshots: Grafana dashboard snapshots for latency, error-rate, and throughput (include time range +/- 2 minutes around alert).
2. Export recent traces for the correlated trace IDs (top 5 errors by frequency).
3. Pull the latest router logs and model-serving logs for the affected model IDs (tail -n 500).
4. Record container/node status: kubectl describe pod and node-conditions, and gpu utilization (nvidia-smi) if GPUs involved.
5. KV cache and prefix-cache indicators: cache hit/miss rates, eviction logs.
6. Rate limit / quota events: API gateway logs that show 429/413s.
7. Save request samples (anonymized) that reproduce the failure (redact PII).
8. Note the exact alert IDs, rule names, dashboards and runbook invoked.
9. Create an evidence folder in the incident artifacts bucket with timestamped files and assign read ACL to the incident group.
10. Post a short evidence summary into the bridge notes channel with links to artifacts.

Escalation ladder (when FR cannot progress within 15 minutes)
1. Notify the service owner via PagerDuty: tag with incident severity and "needs expert assistance".
2. If no response in 5 minutes for P0/P1: notify SRE lead and product manager via Slack channel #sre-oncall and #product-incidents, and escalate to oncall manager.
3. For customer-impacting or legal-sensitive events: loop in the Customer Success Lead and Legal Counsel (email + Slack).
4. For extended degradations (>4 hours) with SLA exposure: notify Executive on-call and prepare an exec summary for stakeholders.

Bridge setup and operations (boilerplate)
1. Create bridge (Zoom/Google Meet/Slack Huddle) and set title: "INC [ID] – <service> – <severity>".
2. Create a living notes doc and pin to the bridge. Use the incident artifacts template: timeline, evidence links, action items, owner assignment.
3. Assign a scribe to timestamp all actions and decisions.
4. Use the "incident-control" Slack channel for short-form updates and the bridge for decisions.
5. When the bridge is created, post the required fields: incident ID, owner, start time, severity, customers affected.
6. Disable non-essential noisy alerts if they’re causing signal overload (SRE control).

Customer-facing status templates (copy-and-send; customize bracketed fields)
- Initial P0 status (first 15m):
Subject: Redwood Inference – Incident [ID] impacting API availability
Body: We are aware of an incident affecting Redwood Inference API availability impacting [percentage/customers/region]. Our on-call team is investigating. We have opened an incident bridge and will provide an update within 30 minutes. Impacted customers: [list]

- Hourly update (P0/P1):
We continue to investigate. Current observations: [short bullet list]. Next steps: [action owners and ETA]. We will provide the next update at [time].

- Resolution:
Subject: Incident [ID] resolved — Redwood Inference service restored
Body: Root cause: [brief summary]. Mitigation: [what we did]. Impact: [customers, duration]. Next steps: post-incident review scheduled for [date/time] and contact [CSL email] for specific customer concerns.

Post-incident handoff and postmortem gating
- Handoff checklist for IC to postmortem owner:
  - Confirm incident is stable for 24 hours and rollback windows closed.
  - Ensure evidence bucket contains all artifacts and that links are persisted.
  - Tag postmortem owner and set a 7-day draft due date.
  - Record 3 candidate corrective actions (one technical, one process, one people/training).
- Postmortem structure (required fields): event timeline, impact analysis, root cause hypothesis and evidence, mitigation and verification steps, action owner and due dates, communication timeline.

Game day scenarios and cadence
- Twice-yearly game day focused on: KV cache pollution, burst-throttling (rate-limit induced failures), and multi-region failover.
- Quarterly tabletop: senior leaders + SRE + CS practice executive comms and credit/SLA decisions.
- Training exercise template: 1-hour simulated P1 with pre-seeded alerts, scribe review, and 30-minute retro.

SLOs and metrics to track for continuous improvement
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): target P0 < 1 minute, P1 < 5 minutes.
- Mean time to evidence: target < 15 minutes for P0/P1.
- Mean time to restore (MTTR): targets by severity; track by rolling 90-day median.
- Postmortem completion rate: 100% for P0/P1 within 7 days.

Templates and artifacts (quick links)
- Incident artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/[incident-id]/
- Evidence capture checklist (copyable): paste into bridge notes when standing up.
- Customer status message matrix (short-hand): use the templates above and localize as required.

Related guidance and references
- See: incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework for postmortem rubric and approval flow.
- See: first-responder-playbook for immediate triage commands and CLI snippets.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets
- Grafana snapshots: use the "Share > snapshot" flow and copy the link into the evidence folder.
- Retrieve recent traces (example):
  - curl -s "https://tracing.internal/api/traces?service=<svc>&from=<t1>&to=<t2>" > traces.json
- Pod diagnostics (k8s cluster):
  - kubectl get pods -n <ns> -o wide
  - kubectl logs <pod> --since=15m | tail -n 500 > pod.log
- GPU diagnostics: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv

Ownership and maintenance
- Document owner: Asha Patel (oncall practice lead).
- Review cadence: annual review; after any P0 postmortem or major SLA incident.
- Feedback: file requests/updates in the Incidents doc backlog in the Eng Platform board.

End of playbook
